answer.summary: Revolut gives product teams substantial autonomy to build and choose their roadmaps, while founders retain visibility and intervene through reviews and screen checks. Zlokazov describes this as accountability and a last line of control—not micromanagement—which helps the company build many products at scale.

sections.heading: Autonomy with accountability
sections.content: Product owners are meant to be fully autonomous. They can defend their roadmap with the reasoning behind their decisions and may retain leadership’s trust to keep building even when metrics are not yet there. Teams present weekly outputs, where founders can provide steering or challenge decisions.

sections.heading: Leadership oversight without micromanagement
sections.content: Founders maintain a full view of the work and review every screen that ships; weekly product reviews and those checks serve as a final control to ensure products make sense and are thoroughly considered. Zlokazov says this oversight is not micromanagement: founders can go deep into details or intervene when necessary, while teams remain autonomous. He says that balance lets Revolut keep building many products rather than cutting opportunities to accommodate founders’ involvement in everything.

judgment.explanation: The answer accurately describes teams’ autonomy to build and shape their roadmaps without micromanagement, alongside founders’ visibility, reviews, ability to challenge teams, and intervention when needed. It also explains that this balance enables Revolut to build many products. The claims are supported by the cited transcript excerpts, and the answer makes no unsupported claim that information is missing.
